However, although tac- rolimus may have a better cardiovascular risk profile than ciclosporin,7,11,12 patients are two to three times more likely to develop diabetes and to have neurological adverse effects.10 Choice of calcineurin inhibitor is therefore strongly influenced by adverse effect pro- files.9,13,14 • There is some evidence of synergism between sirolimus and ciclosporin15 and addition of sirolimus to ciclosporin-based regimens may reduce the incidence of acute rejection.4,16 Combining sirolimus with tac- rolimus instead of ciclosporin may be even more effec- tive.4 However, sirolimus may augment the nephrotox- icity of both ciclosporin2 and tacrolimus,5 and its use with full-dose calcineurin inhibitors has been associated with significantly reduced rates of allograft survival.17 In an attempt to reduce the chronic allograft nephropa- thy (see below) associated particularly with calcineurin inhibitors, sirolimus has been given with azathioprine or mycophenolate mofetil, as an alternative to ciclosporin- based protocols. Comparable rejection rates and better renal function have been reported, although the use of sirolimus may increase the risk of cardiovascular-relat- ed morbidity and mortality, and safety has not been es- tablished. Sequential quadruple therapy, in which antibody-based induction therapy is given postoperatively, in addition to triple therapy,2,13 is also used. The antibodies are usually stopped once good graft function is achieved.1 The regi- men may improve long-term graft survival in patients with delayed graft function.18 Polyclonal lymphocyte-depleting antibodies are associat- ed with a low incidence of rejection but evidence of their benefit in terms of graft survival is lacking; rabbit antilym- phocyte immunoglobulin appears to be better than that of equine origin. Use of muromonab-CD3 has declined be- cause of poor tolerability and an increased risk of lympho- proliferative disease.19 The more specific interleukin-2 re- ceptor antibodies basiliximab and daclizumab are widely used and appear to reduce the incidence of rejection epi- sodes without increased toxicity.4,5,18-21 Alemtuzumab has also been used, but data for this drug are comparatively limited.19,22,23 Some consider the interleukin-2 receptor antibodies to be the first-line choice for induction therapy because of their superior safety profile.
